note: Game balance values chosen by our team for gameplay. Not NASA data except where a source is named. First-guess numbers: tune them while playtesting.

oxygen.label: Oxygen
oxygen.source: Daily use based on NASA life-support planning values (about 0.8 kg per person per day). Verify before presenting.

water.label: Water
water.source: Daily use based on NASA's minimum drinking water value (2.5 L per person per day). Recovery is a game number.

power.label: Power
power.source: Game number. Unused power is lost at the end of the day.

power_room.label: Power Room
power_room.job: Player splits the daily power budget between rooms here.

radiation.rule: If sep.found_in_donki is true the particles always arrive. Otherwise roll the random chance for the event level and tell the player it is a simplified rule.

on_empty.rule: When a resource reaches zero: lose a heart, show the explanation, refill one day so the player can fix the mistake.

messages.watch: Solar flare detected! Class {class}, {date}. Radiation may be coming. Prepare the shelter?
messages.radiation_hit: Ouch! Fast particles from the Sun reached the base and the crew was not in the shelter. Thick walls block most radiation, so astronauts hide there during a storm.
messages.radiation_blocked: Safe! The crew was in the shelter and the radiation was blocked.
messages.false_alarm: The particles did not arrive this time. Preparing cost power, but being ready is what real astronauts do.
messages.oxygen_empty: Oxygen ran out! The air machines need electricity, so air comes first.
messages.water_empty: Water ran out! The greenhouse uses water, so watering plants can leave less to drink.
messages.food_empty: Food ran out! Plants need water, light and power to grow.
messages.lucky: The particles did not arrive this time, so Moonie was lucky! But nobody can be sure ahead of time, so real astronauts get ready anyway.

fact_cards.oxygen: We breathe in oxygen to stay alive. The Moon has no air, so astronauts make and recycle their own. The machines need electricity to run!
fact_cards.water: Astronauts need clean water to drink and to grow plants. Water is precious in space, so they recycle as much as they can.
fact_cards.power: Solar panels turn sunlight into electricity. On the Moon, night lasts about two weeks! Power runs the air machines, the plants and the shelter, but there is never enough for everything.
fact_cards.food: Plants in the greenhouse can make fresh food, but they need water, light and power.
fact_cards.radiation: The Sun sometimes throws out bursts of energy called solar flares. Fast particles can follow, and they are dangerous for astronauts. This game uses real solar events recorded by NASA.
fact_cards.shelter: A shelter with thick walls blocks most radiation, so astronauts hide there during a storm.
fact_cards.hearts: Hearts show how healthy the astronaut is. Keep air, water and food up, and stay safe from radiation.

credits.text: Real solar events from NASA's DONKI. Daily oxygen and water needs are based on NASA life-support planning values. All other numbers are simplified for the game.
